analysis:
Documentation-only change in two files, with no code, workflow, protocol or policy change visible in this batch.

1. docs/developer/test.md: adds the 'Startup Performance Recovery' section (head lines 53-78) and the MiMo FP32 preflight-refusal fixture note (head lines 45-51). It lists tests: StartupPerformanceEvidenceTests, ModelCalibrationTests, ProviderLoopCalibrationTests, ProductionModelCalibrationTests, OrdinaryRequestRetirementTests, ModelCalibrationPolicyTests, EngineV2PrefillSamplingTests and PrefillEvidenceRecoveryTests. The tests use loopback, tiny synthetic models and deterministic receipts, with no production endpoints, credentials or real weights. The text states that synthetic timings prove state transitions, not GPU throughput or fleet recovery. This is consistent with the existing test-isolation guidance.

2. docs/operations/provider-release.md: the prepared ProviderCore.version changes from 0.9.20 to 0.9.21 and v0.9.20 is recorded as published 2026-10-12. The text says preparation does not tag, register or publish. It also says the candidate excludes startup health-check timings from throughput learning and enables bounded calibration without a customer job, pinning mlx-swift-lm #305. The release pipeline, signing, R2, registration, App Attest qualification and revocation steps are unchanged, so TB-011 and T-053/T-054 gates are unaffected.

For the next pass: the runtime code behind the calibration behavior (ProviderLoop, ModelCalibration, the ordinary-request retirement API) is not in this batch. Check whether provider-reported throughput or capacity from calibration feeds coordinator routing or billing (TB-002, T-007, T-010, T-029). Also check that calibration inference runs only on provider-local synthetic data and never touches A-001 consumer prompts.

No security regression or threat-model drift is visible from documentation alone.
